bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

news.label: Sin señales

sections.Key Messages:
- Mild and dry conditions expected this afternoon into Friday.
- Snow is expected late Friday and through Saturday, over the
  northern and central Colorado mountains. The Park Range will
  see up to 12 inches while the mountains farther south will
  see up to eight inches.
- An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with
  potential for more mountain snow, but details remain
  uncertain.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 1228 PM MST Thu Nov 26 2026
Models are in good agreement with each other and with satellite
imagery showing the low pressure system moving inland into British
Columbia and a deep trough pushing into the Pacific Northwest. We
already see the high clouds spilling over the ridge as it breaks
down ahead of the trough. Look for the trough to move in over the
Rockies by Friday evening with a couple embedded shortwave systems
passing Friday evening and the stronger Saturday morning.  This
system quickly moves out onto the Plains Saturday evening. Models
indicate ridging building in Sunday, but getting knocked down Monday
by another shortwave system. A deeper, more southern system moves in
over the Desert Southwest through mid next week to possibly bring a
return of moisture to the southern mountains, but this far out,
confidence is low.
Expect fair, dry weather today into Friday with high clouds and
light winds across the region. Clouds will move in from the
northwest Friday with a few light snow showers across the northern
Colorado mountains through the afternoon. Snow increases over the
Park and Elkhead mountains Friday evening, spreading south into the
Elk and West Elk mountains by Saturday morning. The higher peaks of
the Park Range may see a foot of new snow, but most of the area will
see lesser amounts of 6-12 inches. Issued a Winter Weather Advisory
for the Park and Elkhead mountains for six to 12 inches snow with
locally higher amounts possibly on the higher peaks between 5 PM
Friday and 5 AM Sunday. Farther south across the Flat Tops and the
Central Colorado mountains, look for four to eight inches snow
accumulation by Sunday morning. Issued a Winter Weather Advisory for
these areas for up to eight inches new snow during the same period.
Drier weather returns Sunday, but expect lingering light showers
possible in the mountains. The shortwave Monday brings more showers
to the northern mountains and Flat Tops with a chance in the central
Colorado mountains, but it's too soon to tell how much snow and what
impacts will come with this system. Stay tuned for updates on this.
Then the midweek low moving in over the Southwest will bring
widespread showers across the higher terrain of eastern Utah and
Western Colorado. This one is also too soon to know how much
moisture will accompany it, but it could be a significant storm with
a subtropical fetch of moisture. Stay tuned for updates on this one
too.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 415 PM MST Thu Nov 26 2026
High level clouds will continue to increase across the region
through the period, with ceilings lowering for areas north of
I-70. Ceilings will remain above breakpoints through the next 24
hours, however. Winds will be light and terrain driven. VFR
conditions will prevail.
